## Retrieval relevance

Two measurements are reported over two **different events**. **Selection** is measured on a read-only *seed-memory preview*: which of the scenario's seeded memories the retriever surfaces before any run. **Application** is measured on the *actual memory-mode run*: which memory ids were applied to plans. Application false positives count only seeded memories labelled as never-applicable, so a valid memory *learned during the run* is reported separately and is never counted as a false positive; an applied id that is neither seeded nor reported as learned is surfaced as an unknown (hallucinated) application. A relevant but untrustworthy memory may be surfaced yet correctly blocked from application, so selection precision can be lower than application precision.

## Methodology

- **modes**: {'baseline': 'no retrieval, no learning', 'naive': 'retrieve + apply everything, no validation (research arm)', 'memory': 'retrieve + validate + apply + learn + feedback'}
- **same_conditions**: Each scenario reuses the identical task, environment clone, and attempt budget for all arms; only memory availability/validation differs.
- **prevention_definition**: A run is a 'prevented failure' when an attempt after the first succeeds and at least one retrieved memory was applied to the plan.
- **retrieval_method_comparison**: Similarity-only precision/recall/F1 of each text-similarity method on the labelled seed-memory probes (no ranker weights applied).
- **lifecycle**: Lifecycle labels are derived deterministically from memory age and observed application outcomes; 'projected' advances the clock to the retire horizon.
- **attempt_budget**: Per-scenario max_attempts, identical in all arms.

## Limitations

- Scenarios are simulated with deterministic fault injection; they stand in for real-world failures and are labelled as simulated throughout.
- The agent is rule-based and deterministic; it does not use a general-purpose planning model, so prevention only works for the explicit prevention vocabulary.
- The default retrieval similarity is a lexical hashing embedding, not a trained semantic model. It is reported as 'hashing_embedding'; a neural provider is optional.
- Deterministic tool durations are used for reproducibility; wall-clock time is reported separately and may vary by machine.
- 'Prevented failures' counts attempts that succeeded after applying a memory that matched the scenario's fault category; it is a change relative to the same scenario's baseline, not a causal claim about arbitrary tasks.
- The retrieval method comparison ranks the scenario's seeded memories by similarity alone (no confidence/recency/feedback weights), so it isolates the text-similarity method rather than the full retriever.
- The retrieval method comparison runs on the small set of labelled seed-memory probes embedded in the scenarios, on which textually-related methods can tie; that tie is expected and shows the validation gates, not the choice of similarity function, are what block harmful application. A larger probe corpus would separate the methods.
- The 'naive' arm removes every retrieval gate to model memory applied without validation; it is a research baseline, not a recommended operating mode.
- Lifecycle 'projected' counts advance the clock deterministically to the retire horizon over memories created during the run; they are projections, not observed longitudinal data.
